title: Jordan Sentences Three Men to Death Over Karak Church Shooting That Killed Nine
dek: Jordan’s State Security Court convicted three men of the Oct. 23 attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate. The ruling can be appealed and will get automatic review.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Street view of Al-Karak, Jordan, the city in the governorate where the church attack took place (file photo)

keyPoints: Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for the Oct. 23 attack on St. George’s Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud village, Reuters reported, citing the state news agency Petra.
The attack killed nine people, according to Reuters and AP. Reuters reported that 34 people were also wounded.
The court convicted the men of terrorist acts resulting in death, possessing weapons for terrorist purposes and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group.
The ruling is subject to appeal and automatic review by the Court of Cassation, Petra said.

Jordan’s airstrikes on southern Syria, launched later on the day of the arrests, killed civilians, Syrian authorities said; Jordan acknowledged civilian deaths, and the two countries agreed to form a joint security committee.
body:
Jordan’s State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported, as carried by Reuters. The Associated Press, in its Sunday Mideast roundup, also reported the sentences and the Oct. 23 shooting at St. George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hamoud, north of the city of Karak.

## The attack and the arrests

Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at the church on Oct. 23, Reuters reported. Authorities said 34 people were also wounded. Reuters described the attack as rare against Jordan’s Christian minority.

Security forces arrested the three men on Oct. 26 after a shootout at an abandoned house in Karak, according to the Public Security Directorate, as reported by Reuters. All three were wounded in the shootout, and no security personnel were injured.

## The verdict

The court convicted the men of offences including carrying out terrorist acts resulting in death, possessing weapons and ammunition for terrorist purposes, and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group, Reuters reported. The ruling is subject to appeal and automatic review by the Court of Cassation, Petra said, so the sentences remain open to challenge through those steps.

The verdict came in the same Sunday Mideast roundup that carried reports of other regional developments. AP reported in that briefing that Houthis said they had freed around 600 detainees captured in the latest escalation of fighting in Yemen, and that Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed it struck a radar system at an American helicopter base in Bahrain. The U.S. military command did not immediately comment on that claim.

## Regional fallout

Jordan, a U.S. partner in the fight against extremism, launched airstrikes on southern Syria later on the day of the arrests against groups it linked to the church attack, Reuters reported. Syrian authorities said seven people, including three children and a woman, were killed in those strikes. Jordan later acknowledged that its airstrikes had killed civilians in Syria, and the two countries agreed to form a joint security committee to review the incident and its consequences.

Meridian has not independently verified the court’s findings beyond the reporting cited here. Defence and appeal steps remain open, and the Syrian casualty figures come from Syrian authorities as reported by Reuters.
